correctness.rationale: At maximum combined length minimality is equivalent to disjoint unique embeddings. The coordinatewise min/max lemma verifies the local no-replacement test; modulo-q transition graphs for q=3,4,5 yield, by inductive path counts, exactly 1, 2^(4k-1), and F_(10k-1) for every k>=1. All boundary conditions and quantifiers are addressed. Direct output-minimality enumeration and independent grid DP corroborate finite cases.

value.rationale: The maximum-length stratum is a natural, nontrivial extremal invariant of minimal common supersequence enumeration. A canonical family of periodic one-step shifted inputs exhibits a sharp transition from unique output to a binary branching law to Fibonacci growth across the first three nonbinary alphabet sizes, and the exact lattice-path model explains the behavior. These counts can benchmark general enumeration algorithms without requiring a larger downstream theorem.
